steps.title: Sort by two columns
steps.prompt:
ORDER BY can take more than one column.
Rows tie on the first column, then the second breaks the tie.
steps.task: Try typing: SELECT id, sale_id FROM sale_items ORDER BY id, sale_id;
hints: Start with SELECT id, sale_id FROM sale_items.
Add ORDER BY id,
Then the tie-breaker sale_id.
Write: SELECT id, sale_id FROM sale_items ORDER BY id, sale_id;
steps.expected_sql: SELECT id, sale_id FROM sale_items ORDER BY id, sale_id;
steps.memory_trick: List keys left to right: primary, then tie-breaker.

steps.title: Sort by two columns
steps.prompt:
ORDER BY can take more than one column.
Rows tie on the first column, then the second breaks the tie.
steps.task: Try typing: SELECT sale_id, id FROM sale_items ORDER BY sale_id, id;
hints: Start with SELECT sale_id, id FROM sale_items.
Add ORDER BY sale_id,
Then the tie-breaker id.
Write: SELECT sale_id, id FROM sale_items ORDER BY sale_id, id;
steps.expected_sql: SELECT sale_id, id FROM sale_items ORDER BY sale_id, id;
steps.memory_trick: List keys left to right: primary, then tie-breaker.

steps.title: Skip 2 then take 2 of id
steps.prompt:
OFFSET skips that many rows before LIMIT starts counting.
Together they page through a long list.
steps.task: Try typing: SELECT id FROM sale_items ORDER BY id LIMIT 2 OFFSET 2;
hints: Start with SELECT id FROM sale_items.
ORDER BY id first.
Finish with LIMIT 2 OFFSET 2.
Write: SELECT id FROM sale_items ORDER BY id LIMIT 2 OFFSET 2;
steps.expected_sql: SELECT id FROM sale_items ORDER BY id LIMIT 2 OFFSET 2;
steps.memory_trick: LIMIT = how many; OFFSET = how many to skip.
